pages.text: Atlas Cloud offers an annual subscription of $24,000 for 100 seats. The quote covers the core workspace and standard integrations.
A mandatory, one-time implementation fee of $4,500 covers migration, configuration and administrator training. This charge is excluded from the annual subscription.
Premium support costs $3,600 per year and is required for the four-hour response SLA. Standard email support is included without a response-time commitment.
Atlas includes 1,000 GB of storage. Additional storage is billed at $0.12 per GB per month. Overage is excluded from the base quote.
Atlas may increase subscription prices by 7% at annual renewal. Cancellation requires written notice at least 60 days before renewal.
Bloom Systems charges $27,600 annually for 100 seats. The subscription includes all standard connectors and audit logs.
Bloom includes implementation and migration at no extra cost. The one-time implementation fee is $0.
Bloom includes 24/7 premium support with a four-hour response SLA in its subscription. The additional annual support charge is $0.
Bloom includes 2,000 GB of storage. Additional usage is charged at $0.08 per GB per month. Data export is included.
Bloom caps annual subscription increases at 3%. Customers may cancel with 30 days of written notice before renewal.
Cobalt Works charges an annual base subscription of $21,600 for 100 seats. Custom integrations are quoted separately.
Cobalt requires a one-time implementation fee of $6,000 for migration and provisioning. This fee is not included in the advertised subscription.
Cobalt premium support costs $4,800 per year for a four-hour response SLA. Standard support has a two-business-day response target.
Cobalt includes 500 GB of storage. Additional storage is charged at $0.18 per GB per month. A termination data export costs $750, excluded from ongoing operating cost.
Cobalt may raise subscription prices by 10% at renewal. The contract automatically renews unless cancellation is received 90 days in advance.
The security policy requires AES-256 encryption at rest for all customer records and backups.
The minimum transport encryption version is TLS 1.2. Legacy protocols must be disabled.
Security administrators review employee access every 90 days and revoke inactive grants.
Suspected security incidents must be reported to the security team within 1 hour of discovery.
Encrypted daily backups are retained for 35 days. Restoration drills take place quarterly.
Every new teammate receives an onboarding buddy for the first 30 days.
The onboarding equipment budget is $1,500 per new employee, subject to manager approval.
New teammate orientation takes place every Monday at 10:00 in the company timezone.
The probation review is scheduled after 90 days of employment.
Security and privacy training must be completed within 14 days of joining.
The daily meal allowance for business travel is $65. Itemized receipts are required.
The standard hotel reimbursement limit is $220 per night, before applicable taxes.
Travel expense claims must be submitted within 30 days of the trip ending.
Single expense claims over $500 require department head approval.
Approved expense claims are reimbursed within 14 days of final approval.
The internal search beta is scheduled for November 20, 2026. This is a planning date, not a delivery guarantee.
The mobile pilot is planned for December 5, 2026, with 50 internal participants.
The product roadmap sets WCAG 2.2 AA as the accessibility target for new interfaces.
The Q4 search initiative has an allocated capacity of 24 engineer-weeks.
The search beta cohort is limited to 150 users during the first rollout.
The standard API rate limit is 120 requests per minute per authenticated workspace.
API clients should use a request timeout of 30 seconds and retry transient failures with jitter.
Failed webhook deliveries are retried for up to 5 attempts with exponential backoff.
The maximum JSON API request payload is 10 MB. Large files use the upload endpoint.
Production service tokens must be rotated every 60 days. Never place tokens in browser code.
The proposed search platform uses 384-dimensional embeddings for its baseline vector index.
The baseline chunking strategy uses an overlap of 80 tokens between adjacent chunks.
The reranker receives the top 30 candidates after reciprocal rank fusion.
The answer context includes up to 5 passages after relevance and permission filtering.
The initial ingestion deployment allocates 4 workers for document processing.
Critical customer incidents have a first-response target of 15 minutes during staffed hours.
Unresolved high-priority incidents escalate to the incident commander after 2 hours.
The customer satisfaction target is 92% positive responses. This is a target, not a measured result.
The daily support handoff takes place at 09:00 UTC using the shared incident log.
The operations team reviews recurring incidents weekly and assigns remediation owners.

The synthetic Q3 2026 snapshot records total operating expenses of $1,680,000.

The synthetic Q3 2026 forecast estimates a cash runway of 18 months at current burn.
The synthetic Q3 2026 operating expense variance is 4% above budget.
The synthetic search research study included 24 participants from four departments.
Each customer research interview lasted approximately 45 minutes.
In the synthetic study, 83% of participants preferred answers with direct source references.
The synthetic study found a median search frequency of 8 searches per day.
The most frequently mentioned pain point was fragmented knowledge across disconnected tools.
